B. Is this measure already running in West Uusimaa wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how much?
Measure: Nurse navigator for every suspected lung cancer. A named nurse books and chases every test, calls the patient, prepares the MDT and removes waiting between steps from referral to first treatment.
effect_summary_en: The 2026 scoping review of 13 studies says navigation was consistently linked with faster first treatment, but its abstract gives no pooled difference against usual care, so the assumed 15% cut is not measured.
supported_en: A 2026 scoping review of 13 studies (Japan Journal of Nursing Science) found navigation consistently linked with faster first treatment.
not_supported_en: No page shows the 15% (0–30%) relative cut in days or any effect on the time from first symptom.
in_use_summary_en: There is no public sign of a named nurse navigator for suspected lung cancer at Länsi-Uusimaa (LUVN) or HUS; HUS's pathway page only says patients meet a nurse for guidance at the first visit and that a team of HUS specialists gives a treatment recommendation when needed.
summary_en: HUS's lung cancer pathway page (updated 15.06.2026) describes a guidance nurse at the first visit and a team of HUS specialists that gives treatment advice when needed, but not a named navigator who books and chases every test; no LUVN page on this was found. A 2026 scoping review of 13 studies found navigation consistently linked with faster first treatment but gives no pooled effect size, so the 15% assumption is not shown.
unanswered_en: I found no LUVN or HUS page on a lung cancer coordinator or navigator nurse, and no measured effect size of navigation compared with usual care.
